title: Aegerion / American Equity / AMC / Aena / American Eagle — Denominator Quality, Security Selection and Value Crystallization V9

notes: AEN 2004, AENA 2015, AEO 2007, AEO 2008, AEO 2021 and AEOS 2005 raw Short -> actual Long.
AEGR is not a common-equity idea; it is a Long in Aegerion 2.0% senior unsecured convertible notes due 2019.

AEGR entered Chapter 11 in 2019. The disclosure statement estimated approximately 80.7% recovery for Class 6B Other General Unsecured Claims, which included the convertible-note claims, but exact realized IRR requires security-distribution dates and market values.
AEL's final payoff is best anchored to the 2024 Brookfield Reinsurance acquisition completion value of $56.50 per share rather than a stock-chart endpoint.
Legacy AMC ticker AEN is distinct from today's AMC ticker; the 2004 common was cashed out at $19.50/share.
AEO/AEOS vintages are preserved as separate idea units because entry denominator, catalyst and horizon differ materially even though the economic franchise is the same.
AEOS 2000 and 2005 lack source-DB performance rows; third-party historical prices are used only as magnitude/target-hit cross-checks, not as exact realized IRR.

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: 2017 breakeven/refinancing thesis는 실패해 Chapter 11에 갔지만 Class 6B estimated recovery 약 80.7%로 common과 달리 claim value는 상당 부분 남음
meta.key_mechanism: discounted unsecured claim retained recovery value despite enterprise failure, but senior layering and burn changed the path

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: Brookfield partnership·대규모 buyback이 현실화되고 2024 $56.50/share transaction으로 $27 entry가 약 2.09x crystallize
meta.key_mechanism: reinsurance and higher-return assets released capital while discounted buybacks compounded per-share value and Brookfield ultimately crystallized value

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: 약 $15 entry의 $19~20 base/upside가 2004 $19.50 cash takeout으로 9개월 내 직접 실현

batch_lessons: A company bankruptcy does not imply a zero bond recovery; entity, seniority and new-money priming must be analyzed before the company narrative.
Corporate-action consideration is often a cleaner realized-value anchor than a stock-chart endpoint.
AEL shows that discounted buybacks can compound an insurance transformation when reinsurance releases capital and a strategic counterparty validates the asset model.
Aena shows that denominator growth and deleveraging can drive a rerating even without heroic multiple expansion.
The four AEO vintages show that a low multiple has no standalone information: peak, trough-normalized and forward-target denominators produce very different outcomes.
Insider buying is useful evidence of alignment but is not a cycle-timing guarantee.
A growth option is safest when the core business already covers much of the purchase price; it is riskier when a high standalone multiple and separation probability are required.
Retail turnaround returns must preserve timing: a correct five-year business call can still be a poor one- or two-year investment.
Temporary-dislocation retail ideas should use inventory, category comps and balance-sheet runway as fast falsifiers.
Exact bond or merger IRR should not be manufactured when settlement dates, distributed-security values or daily entry prices are incomplete.
